summary: Introduces Jinja tests, which evaluate expressions to True/False for comparisons (vs filters for data manipulation), can be used in select/map, run on the control node, and Ansible adds more.
questions: What's the difference between a Jinja test and a filter?

answer_card.title: What tests are
answer_card.answer_md: Tests evaluate an expression to **True or False** and are used for comparisons; filters manipulate data. Tests can also drive list filters like `select()`. They run on the **control node**. Ansible adds its own tests on top of Jinja's built-ins, and you can write your own.
